tasteReview.evaluator: separate Sonnet evaluator agent, SITE-31, session 019RdEm6 — three independent scorings of one capture run of the blog template rendered on its best-performing published post; no page code read, no live page opened

shotSpec.capture: scripts/take-route-shots.mjs, device scale 1, palette-quantized, consent banner and dev badge suppressed. The exemplar post predates the SITE-31 spec (no Questions block, no sourced figures); the score is for the TEMPLATE the eleven new guides will render on.

tasteReview.beats: I did not open any competing page this session (no browser/fetch was used) — I have no basis to name a page we beat or lose to, and I am not inventing one.
tasteReview.scoringNotes: Three genuinely separate looks at the same four PNGs. Pass 1 (52) took the type/chrome at face value: Amboqia H1, correct navy/cream tokens, clean nav, and marked it down for the obvious flat prose body. Pass 2 (44) moved down after I actually measured the hero photo: body-desktop.png is anchored on <article> and is 100% photograph for the full 900px capture, zero text — meaning the same image that runs ~280px tall (34% of viewport) on mobile375 is upwards of ~1075px tall on desktop (back-solved from the mobile aspect ratio), so a desktop reader clears a full screen of unlabeled scenery before any word of the article, and I weighted that harder plus the fact that the one number in the visible prose ('about 1,700 year-round residents') carries no visible source treatment at all. Pass 3 (57) moved back up after pixel-sampling contrast and confirming the eyebrow label is full navy (16,39,66, ~14:1) and the byline is a correctly-mixed navy-70 token (~5.5-5.8:1, comfortably AA) — the token discipline is genuinely clean, which argues for crediting craft/design more than pass 2 did. Spread is 13 points (44-57), median 52. The swing is entirely about how much weight to give 'good bones' (chrome, type, token discipline) against a body that shows zero interaction and zero figure/citation treatment in every one of the four captured regions — none of the three passes found anything to change that latter judgment, only how much the former should offset it.
tasteReview.evidenceLimits: The two 'body' shots are anchored at the top of <article>, and on desktop that lands entirely inside the hero photograph — I measured zero non-photo pixels anywhere in body-desktop.png, so I cannot see a single body paragraph, heading, figure, or interactive element on desktop from this record; every desktop craft judgment below the hero is inference from the mobile shot, not direct observation. None of the four shots scrolls far enough to show the Related Homes ledger (V3Ledger), the Quiet block, a Questions/FAQ block, or place-page links, all of which are blocking required imports per parity.json but are entirely absent from evidence — my interaction and honesty scores are conservative specifically because of this blind spot, and the reality below the fold could be meaningfully better or worse. I checked the full byline row at native resolution for a ShareButton (also blocking-required) and found no icon anywhere in it; it may render further down, in a region none of these shots reach, so I cannot confirm it exists on the page at all versus confirm it is merely uncaptured. No loading, empty, or error state is captured — all four shots are one hydrated success state. Static PNGs cannot show hover states, focus-ring visibility, scroll-bound motion, or true 44px tap-target sizing (only approximate from layout pixels). Separately, and not a scoring factor: the task brief names the exemplar as 'Sunriver Year-Round Living: What It Costs in 2026,' but every shot renders the title 'Sunriver Year Round Living vs Vacation Home' — a different post entirely. I scored the four shots as given rather than resolve the naming mismatch.
tasteReview.instrumentNotes: FIRST MARK for this class. Before 2026-09-09 the blog route had no parity.json and no tasteReview, so SITE-31's accept clause ("rises above its previous mark from the same instrument") had nothing to rise above; this receipt is the baseline the next blog round compares to, on the same evaluator model, rubric and a re-captured record set. Within-call spread here: 13 points (52, 44, 57); across the place classes this instrument spread 5-13 within one call on 2026-09-08, so a few points either way is noise.
tasteReview.topThree: 1) Give sourced numbers in prose a visible trace — a footnote/source-line pattern or promotion into an Instrument-style stat — because the incoming eleven posts are defined by 'every number carries its window and sample size' and the template currently has zero apparatus for this; right now a verified stat and an invented one would render pixel-identical. 2) Fix the desktop hero's height — it is measurably a full viewport-plus of undifferentiated photography (confirmed: 900px of pure photo pixels, zero text) versus a well-proportioned band on mobile — so the desktop reader's entire first scroll is spent on unlabeled scenery. 3) Put at least one interactive element in the article's open fold (hover citation, scrubbable stat, toggle) — across all four shots there is currently none, which is the rubric's interaction floor (15 points), not a passing mark, and it is the one criterion no amount of good typography can offset.

defects.finding: The one numeric claim visible in the prose ('Sunriver is both a full-time residential community, with about 1,700 year-round residents...') has no source trace of any kind near it — no footnote marker, no hover citation, no source line, no promotion into a figure/stat component. The template offers no visual apparatus to make a sourced number look sourced. Smallest fix: a hairline source-line under any paragraph carrying a stat ('Source: SROA, 2026'), or lift the number into an Instrument-style stat display with its trace, matching §0's own enforcement language.

body-desktop.png (anchored on <article>) is 100% photograph across the full 900px capture — measured, not eyeballed: every sampled pixel in the bottom 40 rows is pond-water color, none are cream/text. Back-solving from the mobile crop's aspect ratio (~280px tall at 375 wide), the same image renders at roughly 1075px tall at 1440 wide — a full screen and then some of undifferentiated stock/drone photography before a single word of the article appears, while the identical image is a modest, well-proportioned band on mobile. Smallest fix: cap the hero to a max-height (e.g. 60-70vh) independent of source aspect ratio so headline or first paragraph is visible in the same scroll gesture on desktop.

Zero interactive affordance appears anywhere in the article region across all four shots — no hover state, scrubber, toggle, or expandable, only plain paragraphs and one bare H2. Rubric weight on interaction is 15/100 and the standing rule is 'every data section rewards a hover, tap, scrub, or toggle' — the visible portion of this template gives the reader nothing to do. Smallest fix: put one interactive primitive in the open fold, e.g. a hover-revealed citation on the first sourced number, or an inline stat-tile with a sparkline drawn from Instrument.

The full-bleed golf-course/pond photo carries no caption, credit, or location label anywhere in evidence. parity.json's own competitiveTarget names exactly this pattern ('a portal's neighborhood article: stock photo, listicle, no figure with a source') as the thing to beat, and as rendered the opening is indistinguishable from it. Smallest fix: one caption line under or over the image naming the place and doing editorial work ('The Woodlands course, looking toward the Cascades') instead of decoration.

ShareButton is a blocking-required import per parity.json but is not present anywhere in the byline row — checked pixel-by-pixel at native resolution across the full row width, nothing rendered. Either it fails to render on the open, or it lives somewhere none of these four shots reach; either way it delivers zero value to a reader who does not scroll to wherever it actually is. Smallest fix: place it visibly beside the byline, where editorial convention already expects it.

'COMMUNITY SPOTLIGHTS · CENTRAL OREGON' is properly cased (not a raw slug) but reads as internal taxonomy vocabulary with no visible function — not tappable as far as any shot shows, not filtering, not linking anywhere. Minor next to the others, but it is empty ornament on a page whose thesis is data-first. Smallest fix: make it a real filter link to the category archive, or cut it if it does nothing.

bannedTells: Walls of text — the visible article body is multiple consecutive paragraphs of prose under a bare H2 with no figure, image, map, or interactive element anywhere in the captured region, matching the rubric's definition verbatim.
